sections.h2: Ways to sell quickly in DeKalb
sections.html:
Cash from a purchaser who takes the property exactly as it stands usually closes fastest, because no bank appraisal or repair list stands in the way. Hiring a broker or going it alone can also succeed, though both wait on showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval.

  • A broker fits a sound house and an owner with time to spare.
  • Going private fits a seller who is at ease with contracts, disclosure forms and setting a price.
  • A straight cash sale fits probate homes, occupied rentals, neglected properties and owners racing a moving date.

DeKalb draws an unusually mixed set of purchasers. A university town with warehouses near the interstates attracts owner-occupants, landlords and investors alike.

DeKalb has 40,467 residents, and renters outnumber owners. Northern Illinois University, with about 20,000 students, is the largest employer, which keeps a steady pool of rental demand. The median age is just 27.7. Of 16,629 housing units, 8.2 percent stand vacant.

With owners living in just 42.1 percent of units, a large part of the stock is rental. An investor buyer will likely want copies of leases, a rent roll and proof of city registration.

Pricing a DeKalb house means looking at both groups of buyers. A family buying to live in it cares about the roof, the basement and the school district. An investor cares about rent, vacancy and what the city will require. Ask any cash buyer how they arrived at their number, and ask for the closing date in writing.

An average year brings 37.25 inches of precipitation and 33.1 inches of snowfall, and the wettest months are May and June.

The Kishwaukee River crested at 15.27 feet on August 24, 2007 and flooded parts of town. If your house is near the river or has ever taken on basement water, say so up front and keep your repair receipts. Buyers' inspectors in this climate look first at roofs, gutters and sump pumps.

When you list or negotiate, keep the paperwork for any sump pump, drainage or waterproofing work. A buyer's inspector will look for water stains, and a folder of receipts answers the question before it becomes a price cut. The disclosure form asks about basement leakage and flooding in any case, so answer it from what you actually know.

sections.h2: DeKalb rental registration and property upkeep
sections.html:
Landlords must register each rental with the city every year. Chapter 10 of the municipal code, revised in October 2022, built the Crime Free Housing Program into that requirement.

  • Registration comes with a security plan aimed at preventing unlawful activity on the premises.
  • Each lease carries a crime free lease provision.
  • Owners attend a class once, then a refresher every year after that, and the city posts the refresher slides online.

Upkeep falls to the Building and Code Compliance Division at 164 East Lincoln Highway, reachable at 815-748-2070. Inspectors apply the International Property Maintenance Code through Chapter 24, mostly by viewing properties from public ground and answering complaints about weeds, trash, snow and ice, and inoperable cars. The city posts annual violation listings, so a seller can learn whether a parcel was cited before a buyer finds out.

Selling a rental? Ask the Crime Free Housing Bureau what your current registration status is and what the next owner has to file.

Deeds go to the DeKalb County Clerk and Recorder on the second floor of the Administration Building, 110 East Sycamore Street, Sycamore, open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. Recording questions go to 815-895-7156. Title companies, attorneys and lenders can record electronically, and mailed or hand-carried paper still works.

The Recorder's fee schedule is $74.00 for a standard letter-size deed and $94.00 for a larger page. Transfer stamps are 50 cents per $500 of value for the State and 25 cents per $500 for the County, and the state declaration is filed through MyDec. A deed must show who prepared it, where to return it, where to send tax bills, the PIN and the street address.

The Treasurer mails a single bill around May 1 with two coupons. Due dates land near June 1 and September 1 each year. Each month of delay adds 1.5 percent, and taxes still open after the second installment can be sold, with redemption handled by the County Clerk at 815-895-7149.

A buyer who receives a bill in a former owner's name can download a copy from the county's online portal, and a seller no longer holding title should pass the bill along. Treasurer's office: 815-895-7112.

Ask the title company to show how the current year's bill is split at closing. Since the bill arrives in May and is paid in two coupons, a sale in the second half of the year usually means the first coupon is already settled and the second is prorated between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Selling a DeKalb house with tenants
sections.html:
Because renters outnumber owners here, many sellers have someone living in the house. Buyers who purchase occupied rentals usually want the same short list, so assemble it before you take calls:

  • Signed leases and any addenda, including the crime free lease provision.
  • A rent roll showing what each tenant pays and when.
  • Security deposit records, so the title company can credit the deposit to the buyer.
  • Proof that the rental registration with the city is current.
  • Tenant phone numbers, in case the buyer wants a walk-through.

Tell tenants about the sale in writing and keep access reasonable. A cash buyer will often take the house with the tenants in place, which spares you from a turnover, but the price will reflect the leases, the rents and the condition of the unit.

sections.h2: Paperwork a DeKalb seller should collect
sections.html:
A brief checklist keeps the closing on schedule.

  1. Find the PIN and street address that must appear on the deed.
  2. Download your newest bill from the Treasurer's portal.
  3. Ask the city about unresolved rental registration or violation notices.
  4. Assemble leases, deposit records and tenant phone numbers for an occupied house.
  5. Ask each lender or lienholder for a payoff letter.

Once a contract is signed, the title company searches the record, drafts the deed, files the state declaration and sends the deed to Sycamore. On closing day you sign the deed and settlement statement, the lender is paid off, and any rent or deposit for an occupied unit is credited to the right party.

faqs.q: Do I register my DeKalb rental before selling it?
faqs.a: Registration is a duty while you own and lease the unit under Chapter 10. Ask the Crime Free Housing Bureau whether yours is current and what a buyer who keeps tenants must file afterward.

faqs.q: Where does a DeKalb deed get recorded?
faqs.a: The DeKalb County Clerk and Recorder, 110 East Sycamore Street in Sycamore, second floor. Title firms may file electronically, and paper filings remain accepted.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax in DeKalb County?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value for the State plus 25 cents per $500 for the County. Filing happens through MyDec, and your closing agent buys the stamps.

faqs.q: When are DeKalb County tax bills due?
faqs.a: Near June 1 and September 1 each year. Late payments add 1.5 percent each month.

faqs.q: Can I sell a DeKalb rental with tenants inside?
faqs.a: Often yes, since investors buy occupied rentals. Hand over the lease, deposit records and contact details, and ask your closing agent how the deposit and current rent will be credited.
